newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo brokerage BEC 1996 turnover up 10-fold.
newsitem.headline: Yugo brokerage BEC 1996 turnover up 10-fold.

text.p: A leading Yugoslav brokerage house Beogradski Eskontni Centar (BEC) reported on Tuesday a ten-fold increase in its 1996 turnover to 3.033 billion dinars in 10,294 transactions.
"The value of the BEC turnover rose 10.44 times while the number of transactions increased 4.66 times over 1995," BEC Managing Director Mirko Galjak said.

"We cannot be satisfied with the structure of our turnover in which only 15.23 percent of transactions were concluded on the bourse and 84.77 percent in the open market," Galjak told the BEC annual shareholders meeting.
BEC also reported a 3.618 million dinars in 1996 profits and said it will pay a 24.13 percent dividend to all of its 46 shareholders. No comparative figures for 1995 were available.

The brokerage also said its total capital stood at 14.99 million dinars, 4.998 million of which was shareholders capital while the remainder resulted from profits and revaluation of the initial capital over last several years. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
